title: Hanging Gardens of Vallejo Street
description: The built in planter at the cantilevered terrace off the kitchen, showing the plantings for color up in the sun at this highest level of the garden.

title: Kitchen at 28 Vallejo St.
description:
Design and construction by Mario Trejo Design.  My friend/client/builder of this spec home is a master at creating both functional and beautiful kitchens and bathrooms in particular.  He added windows and skylights and raised the roof to create a bright sunny space with views out in all directions, including a view of Mount Tamalpais from the kitchen sink.

Mario Trejo Design, 510 418 0823.

title: Front Entry gate and planters
description: This photo shows a straight on view of the entry, with lots of palms, bamboo, grasses and a few succulents.  The blue foliaged grass at the street strip is Agropyron magellanicum, with Erysimum 'Bowles Mauve, Chamaedorea microspadix at both sides of the gate, a Cercis canadensis 'Forest Pansy' at the street just leafing out, and Blackstem Bamboo and a Trachycarpus fortunei palm behind the wall framing the new entry pergola and gate.

title: Aechmea recurvata v. ortgiesii
description: This small bromeliad changes color and turn bright yellow, orange and red as it comes into bloom, and then slowly reverts back to green when done.

title: Portea 'Jungles'
description: Shown here below a Brahea 'Clara' palm, along with foreground plantings of Aeonium canariense v. subplanum.  The plants receive dappled sun except in the winter, when the wall beyond them blocks the low angle sun.  Not exactly fast growing in our cool year round conditions here in Berkeley, but they have grown much better than Portea petropoliteana v. extensa under similar conditions.  I had also tried growing some Androlepsis skinneri under cover of a terrace in this garden, but they still tended to get set back and rot out a bit from the winter cold and damp.  I wish I could have located some Hohenbergiopsis instead, but they just aren't as easy to come by, even thought they are a great large landscape bromeliad for Bay Area conditions.

title: Lower patio and seat wall at 28 Vallejo St Garden
description: This photo was taken when the garden was about 5 months old, and just starting to fill in.

title: Matching raised planters at entry walk
description: The symmetry of these two matching height planters helps to frame this courtyard as a separate space from the entry walk.  Blechnum gibbum dwarf tree ferns are planted at each side, and another Trachycarpus fortunei palm is on the focal axis line.

title: View looking down upon stairs, from dining room window
description: This curving stair case is the only curve in the whole house or garden, and a wonderful counterpoint to the rigid variations on the theme of squares and rectangles throughout the house and garden.

title: Sculptural details
description: A couple of design details were incorporated here to make this terrace more interesting.  Plantings were relegated to built-in low wall planters to give the terrace a less cluttered look, more architectural.  The rear screening wall in the photo is held apart from the house to give more depth, allowing a partial view of the hedge beyond, while screening from view the neighbor's adjoining deck.  The only pots used on this level were massive in scale for this towering Euphorbia ammak variegata, set against the stark white stucco wall for contrast.

title: Concrete, stone and palms at play
description: A contemplative vista from 3 stories up, looking down upon the back garden.  The views out from this third story balcony give a glimpse of the SF Bay Bridge and downtown San Francisco over a forest of Coast Live Oak trees.  I love the interplay of the curves and rectilinear geometry of the hardscape, the subtle mottling of the concrete stain and crackling, against the crisp white walls and turquoise Indonesian inset pebble work.  A view to reach a meditative state of mind...

title: Linaria reticulata and Euphorbia ammak in large pot
Nidularium innocentii
description: This purple foliaged bromeliad is a great plant to use in deep shade where you want some color, and was combined here with Helleborus argutifolius, Phyllostachys nigra, Abutilon and Blechnum gibbum.

title: Closer view of far patio and area below mid level terrace
description: Shade tolerant plantings of Aechmea kertesziae, Aucuba japonica variegata, Impatiens oliveri and Asplenium bulbiferum were used below the terrace.

title: Still life view through a bathroom window
description: It may be hard to notice, but the privacy wall along the side property line was broken to retain the Coast Live Oak tree that was the only vegetation to remain after the remodel.  The gap in the wall is just large enough to allow for future growth, yet still provide privacy and a secure front courtyard.  A Monstera deliciosa climbing vine was placed in a pot behind the built in concrete bench, to eventually climb up the trunk and give a further tropical feel to the entry garden.  The plant with the spotted leaves is also in a pot, and combines Violas with a Farfugium japonicum 'aureo-maculata'.  This window is the opposing view from the bathroom, the other window at the bathtub/shower looks toward the street.

title: Central built-in planter at mid level terrace
description: This was at one time intended to be a reflecting pool and plantings, but I quickly came to my senses and realized that water below a constantly shedding Coast Live Oak tree is not a good mix.

title: Main terrace, stairs at existing specimen live oak
description: This Quercus agrifolia, or Coast Live Oak tree, was the only feature of this backyard before the new landscaping, and originally sat within a sea of grass and weeds on a slope that fell off steeply to the right, and growing on virtual solid rock.  The new expanded terrace and stairs and concrete paving were all carefully located to avoid impacting tree roots or changing the grades within 10 feet of the tree's base.  Plantings were chosen to keep the base of the trunk free of any permanent plants, (some native bulbs were added for spring color), and all additional plants near the oak were selected for their drought tolerance and minimal irrigation needs.  I didn't want to lose this oak to loss from improper conditions, as it was/is the centerpiece of this garden.  The terrace dimensions were designed to step back slightly at one side of the central planter to accomodate the tree trunk leaning in towards the house.  The raised built-in planter nearest the oak trunk has the perfect conditions for the Cymbidium orchid and the Deppea splendens and Blueberry shrub and Fragaria vesca planted there, a few edibles amongst the ornamentals both giving tasty fruit over a long season.  The photo is taken from the upper level cantilevered deck off the kitchen, just visible in view on the left side of the photo.

title: Mahonia lomariifolia with Trachycarpus fortunei palm
description: This composition adjacent the jacuzzi is all about foliage contrast.  Big bold foliage notes come from the glossiness of the foreground plants against the coarse pinnate Mahonia, picking up some similar notes of blue-greens on the palm trunk, which is repeated with the powdery blue trunks of the Blue stemmed Bamboo at the fence, Himalayacalamus hookeriana 'Teague's Blue'.

title: Brahea 'Clara', a most beautiful blue palm
Plantings at Entry Pergola
description: The plantings at the front entry are understated and nearly all green foliage.  Aeonium undulatum, Chamaedorea microspadix, Asparagus retrofractus, and a vining Stauntonia hexaphylla at the wall are the main plants used.

title: Sempervivums and Dyckia platyphylla as ground cover
description: I'm not sure if I would do this combination of plants again, as there may not be enough contrast of foliage color and scale for this to really visually contrast, but it was interesting at the time.  I had no idea that this cultivar of Sempervivum could get so huge, relative to the Dyckia platyphylla.  For whatever reasons, I tend not to use Sempervivums nearly as much as Echeverias, maybe because I don't always get the growing conditions right for the Sempervivums, and tend to rot them out.

title: Walls as sculpture and screening
description: The 8 foot tall wall here was designed to close off the view of the neighbor's deck and backyard beyond, while also acting as a bit of sculpture.  The gap at the house was intentional, to set the wall off as its own element, and bracketed at each side by the built-in planters with matching plantings.

title: Bali, Brazil or Mexico?
description: A garden designed for a bit of fantasy, with tropical vibes surrounded by classic Berkeley hills oak woodlands.  There are links to all three countries, with Balinese stone lanterns, Mexican style inlay pebble work with Indonesian blue pebbles, and lots of palms and tropical looking foliage plants. There's also 4 different palms in this shot.

title: Elegance with foliage
description: The arching form is repeated with all the various plants here, the tree ferns, the palms, even the ground plane Neoregelia bromeliads. The two palms seen here are the stripped Trachycarpus fortunei and the foreground foliage of a Chamaedorea tepelijote.

title: Geraldton Wax Flower, Lotus maculatus 'Gold Flash' and Aloe reitzii
Aeonium undulatum and Astelia nivicola 'Red Gem'
description: A close up photo of the ground plane outside the entry courtyard wall.  A flowering Argentinian bulb, Ipheion uniflorum gives late winter blue flowers at the sidewalk.

title: Plantings behind seat/retaining wall at terrace
description: The majority of plantings in the sun portion of this planter are Sedum palmeri with the pale gray green foliage, darker Sempervivums at the foreground, a large Hohenbergiopsis guatemalensis bromeliad flanking the column, and some Abutilons, an Arenga engleri palm and a Bluestem Bamboo at the fence.

title: Paving patterns and stone lanterns
description: The cast concrete paving here alternates between inlaid Indonesian turqouise river washed pebbles and Sedum palmeri ground cover, and adds an additional color and detail that relates to the house eave rafters which are this same blue green color.

title: Cantilevered Deck off kitchen
description: Up in the sun here, wind protected by the neighbor's redwood trees, with a filtered view of the city and bay bridge, what better place to read the paper with a cup of coffee? The plantings were chosen for year round intense color, and to eventually spill over the railings and create a "hanging gardens of Vallejo Street".

title: Entry Hall tower and landing, looking into living room
description: This tower with its ring of clerestory  windows around the eave and extra height were a design tool chosen by the builer/designer, Mario Trejo of Trejo Designs(510 418 0823), to bring abundant light into the center of the house at both upper and lower levels, and functions well to brighten up the whole house.  The wrought iron railings give an indoor/outdoor feel to this space, and are repeated at the deck and terrace at the back side of the house.  The floor paving also repeats the materials outdoors, but at a slightly different scale, with less dark color and simpler detailing.

title: Chamaedorea tepejilote palm and Blechnum gibbum
Tree top view to the bay from deck off kitchen
description: The view out from the kitchen is enclosed by the surrounding Oak woodlands, but dips down to allow a partial view of downtown San Francisco and the Bay Bridge.  The colorful plantings at the built-in planters have more impact against the deep greens of the Coast Live Oak woodlands.

title: Containers at front entry walk
description: A staghorn fern, a New Guinea Impatiens, some Guzmania hybrid bromeliads and more Chamaedorea microspadix palms are grouped in pots against the wall of the house.

title: My friend John from high school days, visiting on the terrace
description: Wider view of the mid level terrace, and views of oak woodlands beyond.

title: Entry Gate and Arbor at 28 Vallejo St.
Arctotis 'Purple Torch', Aeoniums and Sedum palmeri
Container plantings at entry hall
description: A Rhapis multifida palm and Aglaonema standing sentry at the top floor level of the entry hall.

title: Looking down upon Euphorbia ammak variegata
description: A view one wouldn't ordinarily have of this tree sized growing South African Euphorbia species.  I think this is one very sculptural plant, that looks amazing from almost any angle.

title: Shades of green and white
description: This north facing street side courtyard was kept intentionally monochromatic to give an impression of calm and serenity, as opposed to the outside world beyond the wall.  In reality, this is such a quiet street, hardly any traffic, but the wall was necessary to give privacy to the rooms below street level.  Some less common plants here include Mathiasella blupueroides in bloom, Clerodendrum trichotoum variegata, Stauntonia hexaphylla and Asparagus retrofractus.

title: French drain detail disguised as inset stone paving
description: Instead of using a continuous trough drain inlet at this courtyard, I decided to get playful and instead use Indonesion river washed pebbles set in sand over a perforated pipe drain.  The color of the stone perfectly matches the color of the Trachycarpus trunk stripes, as well as the extended roof eaves at the house.

title: Close up of Spotted Leopard Plant
description: Farfugium japonicum 'aureo-maculata' in pot.
